scope: Independent review of frozen Contexto action-recovery ownership, CaldRece integration, and exact native/projected feedback isolation. No app/test edits or test execution by this reviewer.

findings.evidence: A synchronous lock issues one frozen ticket. Both callback adoption and finish require ticket identity; invalidation releases ownership without allowing old completions to clear a newer flight.

beginAction rejects an already different stored ID before any POST. Recovery checks pointer ownership both before and after one GET. Direct POST responses also pass mayAdoptAction. A same-ID operation from a new screen invalidates the earlier ticket.

recoverOwnedContextoAction accepts only a load callback, invokes the existing one-shot recoverAuthoritative helper and has no mutation or timer. Guess/clue/giveup catch paths call it once. Failed verification enables an explicit GET-only retry and disables further mutations/options.

Recovered authoritative state is adopted wholesale, preserving paid clues and counters. Wins flow through the existing once-per-session score recorder; giveup clears only its own saved pointer and does not write a score. Text is preserved after nonterminal uncertainty and cleared for terminal recovery.

A verified owned 404 returns to setup and conditionally forgets only that ID. A different pointer is never cleared. Local-only rounds remain playable when both saved-pointer observations are null; useActiveGame already catches unavailable-storage access.

Exit preserves the pointer while an action or unresolved outcome may have committed a terminal result, then invalidates the owner. Resumes/new creates also invalidate prior tickets. Old completion callbacks cannot adopt state, write a recovered score, or clear a replacement pointer.

allow_exact_pairs defaults true. Only projected score paths and projected typo filters disable native exact-pair borrowing. Ingredient policy and legacy feedback proxies continue afterward. Projection-specific exact targets still work through their own neighborhood lookup and cannot win.

Three native pairs and two projection-specific exact targets are explicit. Only the new Tort projection uses a fallback anchor that is itself a native exact-pair source. Tort therefore cannot inherit Prăjitură→Cremșnit, while the native Prăjitură guess retains its override.

No session field, score formula, request-size setting or store-bound change. Existing private-answer serialization and typed suggestion filtering remain; defaults are 7200-second sliding TTL, 1000 sessions per game and 65536-byte requests.

validation_observed.method: Read the existing completed native log; did not rerun it.
validation_observed.test_review: Consulted executable helper cases, adapted existing source assertions, browser recovery traffic/state cases, and backend scope/privacy tests. Browser/full-CI completion is not claimed here.

limits: Acceptance binds the exact current source hashes; any subsequent source change needs re-review.
The 193-test result is read from the author’s existing log, not independently executed by this reviewer.
This review does not approve content promotions or assert final browser/full-CI success.
No mutation replay, new persistence layer, network retry schedule or changed server bounds is introduced.
